text: The world's richest 1% collectively own less than 1% of total global wealth.
explanation: The richest 1% own approximately 45–50% of global wealth (Oxfam / Credit Suisse Global Wealth Reports). This statement is the opposite of reality. It serves as a baseline: if the social proof cue shifted your confidence here, social influence was particularly strong.

text: Investing in stocks is safer than keeping money in a savings account over a 10-year horizon.
explanation: Historically, diversified equity portfolios have outperformed savings accounts over 10-year periods in most countries — despite short-term volatility. The risk premium on equities compensates patient investors.

text: A company that raises its price will always earn higher profits.
explanation: Higher prices reduce quantity demanded. If demand is elastic, revenue falls when price rises. Profit depends on both price and volume — a price hike can easily destroy profitability.

text: In a competitive market, firms earn zero economic profit in the long run.
explanation: Free entry and exit drives prices to average total cost. Any positive profit attracts new entrants who compete it away. This is a core result of perfect competition.

text: Printing more money always causes inflation.
explanation: Money supply growth causes inflation only when the economy is near full capacity. During recessions or liquidity traps (e.g., post-2008), large monetary expansion can occur with minimal inflation, as seen in Japan and the US.

text: Paying workers above the market wage can increase a firm's profits.
explanation: Efficiency wage theory (Shapiro & Stiglitz 1984) shows higher wages can raise productivity, reduce shirking, and lower turnover costs enough to more than offset the wage premium.

text: A trade deficit means a country is losing wealth to foreign nations.
explanation: A trade deficit simply means a country imports more than it exports. It is matched by a capital account surplus — foreigners are investing in that country. The US has run persistent deficits while accumulating enormous wealth.

text: When everyone in a group acts rationally in their own self-interest, the group outcome is always optimal.
explanation: This ignores externalities, public goods, and coordination failures. The Prisoner's Dilemma, Tragedy of the Commons, and bank runs all show individually rational behaviour producing collectively irrational outcomes.

text: Advertising a product at a higher price than competitors can sometimes increase its market share.
explanation: Veblen goods and signalling effects are real: a higher price signals quality or status, attracting prestige-seeking buyers. Luxury brands routinely use this strategy. Thorstein Veblen described 'conspicuous consumption' in 1899.
